title: trace-privacy-sampling-and-phi-redaction-notes
body:
Purpose:
This note captures a working set of heuristics and small experiments for making distributed traces safe to store and query when customers require privacy (PHI/PII) constraints — especially for Redwood Private/VPC deployments and regulated customers. Focus: tradeoffs between sampling, anonymization, redaction rules, and dashboard usability.

Context and constraints:
- Hosted API: we can offer richer traces with guarded access and longer retention for support staff under strict controls.
- Private/On-prem: customers often forbid storing raw PII/PHI outside their network or require field-level redaction before any control-plane export.
- Goal: keep traces useful for debugging (span shapes, timing, error locations) while ensuring no raw sensitive data leaves the protected boundary.
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic: recommend minimal computational overhead and clear opt-in knobs.

Design primitives (high level):
1) Sampling tiers:
   - full-sample-local: sample 100% for internal/air-gapped debugging sessions (customer enables).
   - high-fidelity-sample (1-5%): keeps full span names/attributes but runs only inside VPC for short retention windows.
   - metadata-sample (10-25%): keep structural metadata (span name, duration, error flag) but remove or hash attribute values. Good default for customer telemetry export.
   - sparse-probe (0.1-1%): minimal spans used for systemic regressions and SLA telemetry (no attributes).

2) Redaction vs pseudonymization:
   - Redaction: remove field entirely (use when policy forbids storing attribute even hashed).
   - Pseudonymization: deterministic keyed-hash for identifiers (e.g., user_id -> HMAC(key, id) truncated). Enables cross-trace grouping without storing raw ID.
   - Recommendation: prefer pseudonymization for identifiers where customer permits hashed mapping, and redaction for free-text text fields (prompts, responses) unless explicit consent/processing path exists.

3) Field classification heuristic (quick rules):
   - Attributes always remove/strip: raw_prompt, model_input_text, model_output_text (unless explicit opt-in).
   - Attributes to pseudonymize: user_id, session_id, api_key_id, device_id.
   - Attributes safe as-is (low risk): span_duration_ms, gpu_id (grid id), model_name, error_code, quantization_profile, batch_size.
   - Use short allowlist + denylist with regex patterns that can be updated remotely.

Example redaction rules (implementation-ready):
- redaction_regexes: ["\b\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}\b", "\b(?:\d[ -]*?){13,16}\b", "[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}"]
- default_action_for_text_blob: redact
- pseudonymize_keys: ["user_id", "session_id"]
- hmac_method: SHA256, truncate_to: 16 hex chars, key_rotation_period_days: 90

Trace agent changes (cheap ops):
- Add a filter stage before export: classify attributes, apply redaction/pseudonymization based on sample tier and per-customer policy. Keep config small (~10 lines per policy).
- Do not attempt NLP-sensitive-PII detection inline at high volume — expensive and noisy. Offer as an opt-in offline processor for higher-fidelity troubleshooting.
- Metricize the filter stage: emit counters for redactions, pseudonymizations, and discard_rate.

Important metrics to expose (example names):
- obs.traces.received_per_minute
- obs.traces.exported_per_minute
- obs.traces.sample_rate_effective (per-customer tag)
- obs.traces.redaction.count_total (per-field tag: raw_prompt, email, cc, ssn)
- obs.traces.pseudonymize.count_total
- obs.traces.redaction.latency_ms (time spent in filter)
- obs.traces.redaction.failures (parse errors)

Dashboard and alert notes:
- Small dashboard (for eng-sre and product support):
  - Top panel: trace volume in/out and effective sampling ratio (time series + per-customer breakdown).
  - Redaction panel: counts by redaction type (spikes indicate policy misclassifications).
  - Pseudonymization error panel: parsing/failure rate; alert if >0.1% sustained (possible agent bug).
  - Probe panel: ratio of metadata-sample to sparse-probe; sudden drop implies sampling misconfiguration.
- Alerts:
  - P1: redaction.failures > 0.1% for 30m -> page oncall (possible agent crash or new input pattern).
  - P2: exported_per_minute > 3x baseline for a tenant -> investigate runaway export (could be inadvertent full-sample toggle).
  - P3: pseudonymize.count_total == 0 for a tenant that should be pseudonymizing -> warn (config drift).

Retention guidance and export policies:
- Hosted: default retention 30 days for metadata-sampled traces, 7 days for high-fidelity. Customers can opt into longer retention under contract with add'l controls.
- Private: default policy is zero-export of raw text out of customer cluster. Control-plane only receives pre-filtered traces (metadata-sample).
- Logs: keep minimal mapping logs for 7 days for debugging; mapping store must be encrypted and access-audited.

Privacy edge cases and notes:
- Tool-calls and function arguments may carry PII — treat as model_input_text and redact unless explicit allowlist.
- Be careful with span names that include identifiers (e.g., "db.query.user:1234"). Normalize span naming so identifiers are attributes, not part of span name.
- When rotating pseudonymization keys, maintain overlapping key windows for 7 days to allow joinability across traces during rotation.

Operational checklist (short):
- [ ] Add filter stage to trace agent (PR linked above).
- [ ] Ship metric counters and update dashboards (dash skeleton in Confluence).
- [ ] Run a 2-week canary in private-deployments with metadata-sample default. Monitor redaction.failures closely.
- [ ] Document opt-in flow for customers who want full-text support and define legal/data requirements.
- [ ] Add a runbook entry: how to emergency-disable export for a tenant.

Open questions / discussion points:
- Should we offer client-side SDKs that perform redaction before sending spans? Tradeoffs: stronger privacy but more places to maintain rules.
- How much SRM (sampling rate management) do we expose per-tenant? Dangerous to give full control without guardrails.
- Do we need an "inspection mode" where SREs can temporarily see raw text under strict audit? (if so, define audit trail + TTL).

Quick experiment ideas (2–4 week turnaround):
1) Run double-write in canary: keep raw traces locally but export only metadata. After 2 weeks compare investigation success rates for incidents where lack of text impaired debugging.
2) Evaluate a lightweight regex-based extractor vs a small on-host regex+NN model for email/ssn detection: measure CPU and false-positive rate on synthetic prompt corpus.

Authors and next steps:
- Primary: Aisha Patel (obs), reviewed by Martin Chen, Rita Gomez.
- Next: schedule 1-hr sync with product-hosted-api and private-deployments squads to align config defaults and customer-facing language.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep everything opt-out for hosted; default conservative for private.
- Emphasize deterministic pseudonymization since it's very helpful for debugging without storing raw identifiers.
- Avoid heavy NLP PII detection in high-volume hot path; move that to offline tooling.
